meta.title: Contact and visitation chronology — recorded NRE and dates to review
meta.description: First-weekend inventory since 2017, with 2026 dates requiring review and a live separation clock that does not fabricate actual contact hours.

reference.heading: Complaints filed since 2017 — France, Norway, Germany
reference.prefix: Since the judgment of 31 March 2017, I have filed complaints in France, Norway and Germany concerning difficulties exercising my contact rights.
reference.filed: A French complaint document appears below. Filing a complaint does not establish an outcome in any jurisdiction.

note.heading: Note
note.p1: It is said that we are born equal, but we certainly do not give birth equally. The mother has every right to choose where to give birth, without the father’s consent.
note.p2: She knows that whatever she does, she will have sole parental authority, exclusive custody, and the possibility to manipulate the child and use them to obtain rights, power, and money—without ever being held to account.
note.p3: I advise any father against involving social services and filing a complaint against a violent and abusive mother. The result will be that you will never be able to protect your child and they will grow up without you.

timeline.heading: Timeline by year
timeline.lead: Each year shows first weekends of the month. ✗ = recorded historical NRE claim, ✓ = honored or partial, ? = unverified date. Later dates are not automatically criminal findings.
timeline.empty: No weekend matches the selected filters.

location.heading: Location
location.body: 2015 France; since 2017 Norway, Oslo; since 2022 Germany, Frankfurt.

table.heading: First weekends of each month
table.lead: Historic inventory is published through February 2026. From March 2026, dates are generated automatically but their status requires checking the reported German court decision.

exceptions.heading: Reported honored or partial visits
exceptions.lead: Six contact periods are listed in the archives: some involve longer stays, others brief meetings. Holiday dates still need reconciling with the documents.
exceptions.genericDetail: Reported brief meeting: approximately one hour.
exceptions.extendedStay: Longer stay reported; do not add an extra hour on top of holiday time without checking overlaps.
exceptions.otherWeekend: Reported visit: date not yet matched to the separately reported 24-hour weekend.

hours.heading: Time together — estimate from reported periods
hours.net: Elapsed time minus the estimated subtotal of stays
hours.scope: In France, two stays of 7 days and one of 28 days are converted to 24 hours per day of presence; exact dates are not yet matched to the calendar.
hours.source: In Germany, a meeting of around 1 h and a later weekend of about 24 h are reported. In Norway, about three one-hour meetings are reported; their dates remain unknown, so they are included only once in the overall estimate, not assigned to calendar cards.
hours.refresh: The timer updates each second. The month inventory is recalculated from the local Paris date.
hours.suspension: A German contact suspension was reported from 26 February 2026 through 25 February 2027; the operative court order has not been verified here. Later dates are not labeled NRE.
hours.beforeOrder: The March 2017 row predates the cited 31 March 2017 decision and needs review.
hours.intro: According to my account, the scheduled 10 hours per weekend were never respected; rare meetings lasted around one hour.
hours.netHint: Indicative and incomplete: the 42 French holiday days count calendar co-presence, not directly measured contact. Three undated Norwegian meetings are included.
hours.methodology: Calculation method and overlaps to review
hours.contactEstimateHint: France: 42 holiday days counted as 24 h per calendar day (1,008 h). Germany: an approximately 1 h reunion and a 24 h weekend (25 h). Norway: approximately three one-hour meetings (3 h), with dates not yet identified.
